original.amp: Not documented. Modern Nashville country-rock: EL84 and Plexi-style crunch
original.effects: Light compression, slapback, room reverb (style, not documented)
original.notes: Brooks & Dunn's 1991 hit re-recorded with Luke Combs for Reboot (2019), produced by Dann Huff. Described as slightly modernized and a little busier than the original.

recipes.tips: Channel A for the verses: EL84 crunch with snap. Channel B for the big choruses: Plexi-style crunch. Keep it tight and punchy: it's a dance-floor song, so lock in with the kick drum.
recipes.why: Dann Huff's modern country production stacks tight, punchy crunch guitars with a short slapback and a small room. The EL84 sound keeps the twang, and the Plexi adds weight for the choruses.

original.guitar: Session players (not credited in the sources found)
original.amp: Not documented. Modern Nashville lead: clean amp pushed by an overdrive pedal
original.effects: Overdrive, delay, room reverb (style, not documented)
original.notes: Re-recorded with Luke Combs for Reboot (2019), produced by Dann Huff.

recipes.tips: Channel A for the twangy signature licks: a clean Fender pushed by the Tube OD, so it snaps but still has hair. Channel B for the solo: more gain and sustain. Turn the Tube OD off on channel A for a fully clean twang.
recipes.why: Modern Nashville leads usually come from a clean Fender-style amp driven by an overdrive pedal: twangy attack with sustain. A delay just behind the notes fills the space, and a small room keeps it tight.
